news.title: World Cup winners, Fifa legends say Infantino blinded by power
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his now-abandoned proposal to create a commercial body for Fifa tournament rights and sell a 20% stake to private investors. (EPA Images pic) GENEVA: A group of former international players, including World Cup winners and Fifa legends, called on Monday for immediate change at world football's governing body, saying its leadership under embattled president Gianni Infantino had been blinded by power. Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his now-abandoned proposal to create a commercial body for Fifa tournament rights and sell off 20% to private investors.

news.title: Maradona 'Hand of God' football sells for $3.35m at auction
news.lede: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for $3.35m (€2.9m). The sale price achieved by Heritage Auctions in the United States was approximately $6.7m (€5.7m) below the $10m (€8.6m) estimate. The Dallas-based auction house had placed a $2.5m (€2.1m) starting price on the Adidas Azteca ball. Maradona scored twice in Argentina’s quarter-final victory over England on 22 June, 1986 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

news.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ football sold at auction
news.lede: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his ‘Hand of God’ goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for 3.35million US dollars (£2.45m). The sale price achieved by Heritage Auctions in the United States was approximately 6.7m USD (£4.9m) below the 10m USD (£7.3m) estimate. The Dallas-based auction house had placed a 2.5m USD (£1.8m) starting price on the Adidas Azteca ball. Maradona scored twice in Argentina’s quarter-final victory over England on June 22, 1986 at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

news.title: N203bn later, Nigeria’s football crisis deepens
news.lede: Nigeria’s football fortunes have suffered a dramatic decline despite increased government investment in the sports sector, raising questions about whether funding alone can reverse years of structural, administrative and developmental weaknesses in the country’s football ecosystem. For decades, Nigerian football was regarded as one of Africa’s strongest and most productive football systems, powered by the Super Eagles, a competitive domestic league and a steady pipeline of talent playing in leading European leagues. The Super Eagles remain three-time Africa Cup of Nations champions, with their most recent title coming in 2013. Nigeria reached a historic fifth position in the FIFA rankings in April 1994, the highest ever achieved by an African men’s team, while the team has qualified for six FIFA World Cups and reached the round of 16 on three occasions.

news.title: Rodri capture can catapult Barcelona back to very top of European game: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: FIFA hit Argentina with huge fine after Falklands taunt

The Argentine FA has been handed a hefty sanction after its players were seen celebrating World Cup victory over England with a banner relating to the Falklands, while various players and staff have been hit with hefty fines for their involvement in the unsavoury scenes which followed the World Cup final. Argentina knocked England out in the tournament semi-finals, and the build-up to the match was dominated by discussions of the Falklands War.

news.title: India has over 3.4 lakh registered football players: AIFF data
news.lede: New Delhi, Aug 24 (PTI) India has 3,41,862 registered football players, 16,295 coaches and 3,347 referees, the All India Football Federation (AIFF) has told the Central Information Commission (CIC). The figures were furnished by the football federation in response to an RTI application seeking the number of registered players, coaches and referees in India for the 2015-25 period. The application also sought details of the club-wise number of injuries reported by Indian Super League (ISL) clubs during FIFA international windows in 2024 and 2025. It sought information on the achieved and unachieved goals under the AIFF Lakshya 2022 document, Target 2026 and AIFF Strategic Target 2019-22, along with reasons for failure to achieve the objectives and steps taken to meet the unachieved targets.

news.title: Arsenal, Man Utd and England heroes among football icons blasting Infantino
news.lede: A HOST of football legends including World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit and Euros champ Lucy Bronze have shared an open letter turning on Gianni Infantino. The statement was also posted by ex-Manchester United defender Mikael Silvestre, who is on Fifa’s Players’ Voice panel. Infantino is on thin ice in his role as Fifa President following his deeply controversial plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments for £20billion. The Swiss chief, 56, backtracked and U-turned on his money-grabbing scheme but has lost the support of much of football – including some inside Fifa and its member associations and confederations.
